speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. At 8 months old, you are presenting with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension; have you noticed any vomiting, and if so, is it projectile or does it contain bile? Also, has your baby been passing stool normally, or do you see any ribbon-like movements?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby had any blood in his stool, and do you notice if the abdominal mass feels firm and moves with his peristalsis? I will also need to examine the anal region to rule out an imperforate anus. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray_to_check_for_pneumatosis_intestinalis_and_gastric_air. 
Can you confirm if your baby has passed any meconium within the first 48 hours of life, and do you recall the stool ever turning black or tarry?
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung Disease
